title: DOM Algorithm
body:
[[Selecting Nodes]]
[[Modifying Documents]]


---

Every piece of DOM code in this course is the same two steps in the same order:

1. **Select** the nodes: `document.querySelector` / `querySelectorAll`. See
   [[Selecting Nodes]].
2. **Modify** them. See [[Modifying Documents]]. Modifying means one of:
	- change styles (`classList.toggle`, and prefer that over `node.style`)
	- change properties (`textContent`, `value`, `src`)
	- add or remove elements (`createElement` then `appendChild`, instead of
	  `document.write()`)
	- add [[Event Handling]]

Wrapped in a `DOMContentLoaded` listener, because none of the nodes exist until the parser has
finished building the [[DOM]]:

```js
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", init);
function init() { /* select, then modify */ }
```

The one performance rule that comes with it: select **once**, outside the loop. See
[[DOM Performance]]. The one framework observation: [[React]] exists to delete step 1 entirely.
